summary: This benchmark evaluates boundary inference for memory retention under synthetic column faults on an 884,736-cell periodic grid using MLX. The methodology features paired comparisons across fixed, inferred, and oracle ground-truth baselines with bootstrap confidence intervals. While the synthetic setup is highly specialized and the submission is evaluated without an attached code repository, the mathematical formulation, statistical reporting, and experimental controls are sound.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design featuring paired comparisons against both a passive control (fixed regions) and an oracle ceiling (supplied true boundaries).
Comprehensive statistical reporting including paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for retention deltas.
Detailed specification of execution environment, runtime (146.07 s), peak memory consumption (1.79 GB), and hardware configurations.
weaknesses: The evaluation is confined to a synthetic, periodic 3D grid domain with column faults, limiting immediate generalizability to physical memory architectures or standard neural fine-tuning.
Hardware OS metadata contains an apparent anomaly listing 'macOS 27.2', which appears to be a versioning or Darwin kernel numbering typo.
Lacks standalone code submission in the metadata (evaluated under text_only badge), requiring reliance on in-text descriptions.
suggestions: Clarify the practical hardware or architectural analogs of the periodic 3D cellular grid model and detector pulses.
Correct the OS version string in the environment specification to prevent confusion.
Expand on sensitivity to boundary shift magnitudes and non-axis-aligned fault topologies.
